criteria.criterion: A test through Athena::go (the real entry point) shows a job's producer runs in a fresh git worktree with its own target directory under the job's state directory, and that after the job ends both directories are gone, on success and on a failed or rejected job. Run: cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-cli.
criteria.evidence: Five per_job_worktree_* tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs call athena.go(...). A wrapper script records what the producer sees when it starts: workdir == state.work_dir(job), <workdir>/.git exists, CARGO_TARGET_DIR == state.produce_dir(job) (a different path, under the job dir, empty or absent), and no stale file. After go returns, both directories are gone for Landed, Rejected (failing change check), Failed (no edits), a stale start, and a run that ends in an error (the producer deletes .git, go returns Err, the job is not closed). All 5 passed when I ran them. The state.rs guard tests (drop removes both; early error return removes both; stale cleared, checks' target/check kept) passed too. The full suite passed in Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` (1780 tests). The 'worktree' is the producer's one-commit snapshot repository, not a linked `git worktree`; see findings.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs shows the in-flight limit equals floor((free_gb - reserve_disk_gb - check_slots x T) / (T + S)) using T and S from the latest build-measurement record, and that with no record the design estimates (6 GB, 0.2 GB) are used. Run: cargo test -p athena-core disk.
criteria.evidence: These disk.rs tests passed (26 passed in the filter): the_limit_is_floor_of_free_less_reserve_and_check_slots_over_t_plus_s gives 7 for 60/10/1 slot with estimates, 6 for 2 slots, 9 for a measured T=4 GB, S=1 GB, and 1 or 0 exactly at the 22.2 GB edge. the_figures_are_those_of_the_latest_record_not_the_first runs BuildMeasurement::latest over two records in either order and gets the newer one's T and S. with_no_record_the_design_estimates_are_used checks exactly 6_000_000_000 and 200_000_000 bytes and the 'design estimate' source. a_disk_below_the_reserve... checks that the limit saturates to 0 and that T+S=0 does not divide by zero. The planned Athena::start_hold test with a real record in a repository was not added (minor finding).

criteria.criterion: A test shows that when the bound allows fewer in-flight jobs than max_in_flight, the extra start waits rather than failing, and that with max_in_flight = 1 behavior is unchanged and the existing tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and lifecycle.rs pass without edits to their assertions. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: in_flight_bound_* tests (5 passed when I ran them). At max_in_flight=2, 25 GB free and another locked job in flight, go returns Err that downcasts to LowDisk, the job stays Proposed with no Job record, and the hold marker is written. After the lock is released the same job lands. At 40 GB it lands. With no other job in flight (an unlocked leftover does not count) it lands at 12 GB. With the default max_in_flight=1 it lands even with another job running. At drain level the outcome is 'environment: low disk' with failed_item None, the job is still queued, and a second drain lands the same job. The drain.rs diff only appends tests at the end of the file, and lifecycle.rs is unchanged (the empty diff above). The full suite passed in Athena's recorded run.

findings.summary: The per-job 'worktree' is the existing one-commit snapshot repository, not the `git worktree add/remove` the accepted reading assumed
findings.evidence: The reading's assumption said 'Worktree creation and removal run through git worktree add/remove'. The candidate keeps Snapshot::create, which already made jobs/<id>/work per job in the base, and adds a guard that clears the directory at start and removes it on every exit. The change says why (a linked worktree shares history and records/ with the producer) in the CHANGELOG and the design doc, and lists linked worktrees as an open question. The critic accepted this in the round-2 plan, and design section 5's later rebase-at-landing is out of scope. A later job will have to decide this before section 6's rebase works.

findings.summary: The planned test of Athena::start_hold reading a real measurement record was not added
findings.evidence: The plan for criterion 2 included 'a test that calls Athena::start_hold and checks that it reads the pipeline settings and the latest record' from a repository whose records hold a measurement. No such test exists. The path from records.build_measurements to Figures inside start_hold is exercised only with no record (the drain test asserts 'design estimate' in the hold line). The pure functions it composes are tested, so the criterion's wording is still met.

findings.summary: The in-flight probe takes a shared lock on another job's lock file, which can briefly refuse a concurrent command on that job
findings.evidence: The doc comments say this race can happen, and the check is a gate rather than a lock. It cannot bite before build job 10, because only one producer runs until then. A lock-free probe, such as reading the in-flight table A3 writes, could avoid it later.

summary: The change meets the request and all six criteria. Each job's producer runs in its own snapshot repository at jobs/<id>/work, with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR at jobs/<id>/target/produce. A new JobWorktree guard clears both directories at start and removes both on every exit: landed, rejected, failed, a stale start, and a run that ends in an error. I ran five integration tests through Athena::go to show this, and they passed. disk.rs adds the section 5 bound, floor((free - reserve - slots x T) / (T + S)). T and S come from the latest athena.build-measurement/1 record, or the design's 6 GB and 0.2 GB when none exists. Unit tests check the exact integers. At dispatch the bound holds an extra start (LowDisk: the job stays queued, and a later drain lands the same job) only when max_in_flight > 1 and another job is in flight, so max_in_flight = 1 behaves as before. I ran the in_flight_bound tests and they passed. The existing drain.rs assertions are untouched (tests were only appended) and lifecycle.rs is unchanged. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs (1780 tests) passed. Three minor findings, none of which blocks: (1) the 'worktree' is the existing snapshot repository, not the `git worktree` the reading assumed; this is documented with a sound reason and the critic accepted it in the plan. (2) The planned start_hold test with a real measurement record was not added. (3) The lock probe can briefly refuse a command on the probed job, as its doc comments say. Every changed file is on the deliverables list.
